A close reading for the week

“but I done it”

Huckleberry Finn · Chapter XV

After a cruel trick in the fog, Jim tells Huck exactly what the trick has cost him. Huck’s apology is small, delayed and morally larger than the society that taught him to resist it.

It made me feel so mean I could almost kissed his foot1 to get him to take it back.

It was fifteen minutes2 before I could work myself up to go and humble myself to a nigger; but I done it, and I warn’t ever sorry for it afterwards, neither.

  1. 1

    Shame reverses rank

    Jim has just said he could have kissed Huck’s foot for joy at finding him alive; now Huck feels he could kiss Jim’s, out of shame. Jim’s rebuke has overturned the racial hierarchy Huck has been taught, even before Huck can admit it plainly.

  2. 2

    Resistance measured

    Twain gives the delay a number. Seeing the wrong does not make Huck good on the spot: he has to struggle against a social rule that says apologising to Jim would humiliate him.
